mentions.name: useful
mentions.description: A self-hostable tool for building website-based courses as an alternative to video. Course content is written in a simple markup language for slide visuals, extended via a plugin system, and narrated with state-of-the-art CPU-based TTS including voice cloning. It exports a complete website with SEO/social metadata as a PWA that caches for offline use, loads faster than video, uses under 1/10th of the data when served with brotli, and has minimal dependencies. The author plans to prove the concept by publishing website-as-video courses based on their own projects, such as software tools for bass guitar.
mentions.problem: Video is a poor format for delivering course information: the text can't be copied, videos are hard to make, and they are heavy on bandwidth.
mentions.audience: Others creating courses; a stretch goal is letting people turn what they learn via LLMs into low-bandwidth courses so common questions aren't repeatedly asked and 4K videos repeatedly watched.
